title: A walk waits for the panel instead of racing it
goal: Scripted walks fail every so often and pass on the very next run of the same build, always the same shape: the walk looks for a control in the right hand panel and the control is not there yet, or presses one and the press lands where the control used to be. Four separate walks did this in the last three days. A walk that answers differently twice in a row is worse than no walk, because a real break looks exactly like the flake, and every false failure costs a runner a task on the feature in focus. Give a walk a way to wait for the panel to settle instead of guessing a delay, so these stop.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-09-12 on a clean tree.

effects-say-their-reach-walk: failed 1 run in 3 standalone.
  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/effects-say-their-reach-walk.json --no-build
  status failed, [51 expect] FAILED: the control called "Switch" in "Shadow" reads "Shadow, on", not "Shadow, off"
  and in a suite run, the same walk at a different step: [34 expect] FAILED: the control called "Switch" in "Shadow" reads "Shadow, on for 1 of 2", not "Shadow, off for 1 of 2"

effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk: passed 3 of 3 standalone, failed inside
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build effect
  with [32 expect] FAILED: the control called "Twist" in "Border" reads "Border, shut", not "Border, open"
  Step 29 is the second of two presses on the Border's chevron, and step 28's comment already says a full second is needed there because folding a pane slides every heading below it. That points at a press landing mid relayout: the walk waits a fixed time, and when the panel is slower than the wait the press lands where the chevron was.

Both misses are the same shape: a press that finds its target's old position. Worth looking at whether a press should settle the layout before it lands, rather than every walk guessing a wait long enough.

Two more tasks describing the same thing are folded in here and dropped:

  find-out-why-a-walk-passes-on-its-own-and-fails
    "Find out whether a walk starts from the same state first in a batch or last."
    Reproduced 2026-09-12: text-style-walk and text-style-arming-walk fail in a
    15-walk batch with "no menu called Size is in the window" and pass alone.
    Its theory: the probe bundle keeps panel state (scroll position, which
    section is open) in its own settings between launches, so a walk earlier in
    the batch leaves the Text section out of reach. text-style-walk has no
    setup.forget block; style-on-a-copy-walk forgets text, panel, shapes, colour
    and tools.

  find-out-why-the-effects-plus-goes-nameless-whil
    The Add Effect plus is present, right size, right help text, EMPTY name,
    while the panel is still laying out. Sources/Photonz/EffectsListInspector.swift:917
    sets .accessibilityLabel("Add Effect") on it. The log line before the failure
    says the wait never went quiet (14 of 16 slices busy).

387 of 400 passed, 13 failed. Three of the thirteen were run on their own

  $ Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/border-offset-walk.json --no-build          -> exit 0, walk complete
  $ Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/effects-open-into-view-walk.json --no-build -> exit 0, walk complete
  $ Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/panel-edge-column-walk.json --no-build      -> exit 0, walk complete

How they failed in the batch, which is the same shape every time, the panel not
being in the state the walk expects:
  border-offset-walk        step 10: no control called "Shades 2" is in the panel
  effects-open-into-view    step 12: Twist in "Border" reads "Border, open", not "shut"
  panel-edge-column-walk    step 20: no menu called "Add Effect" (the nameless plus, above)
  highlight-one-outline     step 23: Switch in "@border" reads "on", not "off"
  parts-settings-inline     step 24: Switch in "@fill" reads "Fill, on", not "off"
  label-fills-a-row         step 23: "Fixed" is scrolled out of reach
  readout-fields            step 11: "H" is scrolled out of reach
  copies-share-choice       step 61: no control called "Color" in "Fill"; the ones that are: none

Eight of thirteen are a twist left open, a switch left on, or the dock left
scrolled. That is leaked state between walks far more than it is a race, and it
points at one fix for both: a walk starts from a known panel state, and a press
waits for the panel to settle. The panel-edge-column run also printed its own
warning, "[23 setup] put back shapes, panel; changed without saying so: shapes",
so the harness can already see the leak it is not stopping.

This task now owns BOTH halves: the leak and the race. Do the leak first, since
it is the bigger share, then measure what is left.
acceptance: The cause is named in one sentence per half: what state a walk inherits from the one before it, and what a press sees at the moment it misses
A walk starts from the same panel state whether it is first in a batch or last, and that is written up in docs/design/playtest-harness.md
A walk can wait for a control to be present and settled rather than sleeping a guessed number of seconds
